name: Cosmetic peptide injections for facial fat

lead:
Cosmetic peptide injections for facial fat is the idea that injected peptides could reduce fat pads in the face, such as the cheeks or lower face, to leave a leaner, more angular look. It belongs to the wider family of injectable fat-dissolving treatments used to refine facial contours.
No published human trial of peptide injections for facial fat is known. The best-documented injectable in this space is deoxycholic acid (Kybella), approved by the US FDA in April 2015 for fat under the chin, which is a bile acid rather than a peptide.

paras: Injectable contouring treatments in general are delivered by clinicians into the targeted fat area. This article does not describe products, doses or sourcing for peptide compounds.

Injectable products sold outside regulated medical channels carry quality and safety uncertainty, and facial injections can cause swelling, bruising and other local effects. Anyone considering facial contouring is typically directed to licensed clinicians and approved products.

angle.text: The aim is to thin fat pads in the lower face or cheeks without surgery, giving more visible bone structure and a sharper outline.

lead: Cosmetic peptide injections for facial fat refers to the concept of using injected peptides to reduce fat in facial fat pads, aiming for a slimmer, more defined face. It overlaps with the better-known category of lipolytic injections, which are used to reduce small fat deposits.

The established injectable in this area is deoxycholic acid, sold as Kybella, which the FDA approved in April 2015 for moderate-to-severe fat below the chin. It destroys fat cells, which the body then clears over several months.[1] Mesotherapy preparations of sodium deoxycholate with phosphatidylcholine are also used for lipolysis.[1] Neither is a peptide.

No clinical studies of peptide injections for facial fat are known. Registered trials in the facial space instead cover fat grafting and platelet-rich plasma for burn scars, and combined filler-type treatments for volume loss.[2][3]
infobox: Deoxycholic acid (Kybella), chin fat, FDA April 2015

paras: The term is used for injectable peptide products said to dissolve or reduce facial fat. It sits beside deoxycholic acid injections and mesotherapy lipolysis preparations, which are not peptides.[1]

Kybella (deoxycholic acid) was approved by the FDA for reducing moderate-to-severe fat below the chin, with the agency announcement dated 29 April 2015, and works by destroying fat cells that the body then metabolises over several months.[1]

No studies found. Related registered trials address other facial treatments, such as fat injection versus platelet-rich plasma for post-burn facial scars and combined facial aesthetic treatment for volume loss.[2][3]

timeline.event: FDA announces approval of Kybella (deoxycholic acid) for fat below the chin.[1]
